This is the fetch ctr-0006 step (iii), ctr-0001's remaining path and carry-forward [34] had all been asking for since cycle 24. The file is stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py in the src-0017 artefact, retrieved WHOLE via raw.githubusercontent.com and read for which lines EXECUTE, per the ctr-0004 trap in which the IoC evaluator's documented rule turned out to live inside dead triple-quoted string literals. THE EXECUTING RULE, quoted verbatim from the live code. Ground truth per article: article_ttps_set = {ttp.split(' - ')[0].strip() for ttp in raw_ttps if ' - ' in ttp}. Predictions are a dict keyed by technique ID; each key is looked up in a mapping loaded from data/TTP_Mapping.csv, and the scoring set is validated_ttps_set = set(validated_ttps_final.keys()). Metrics: tp = len(article_ttps_set.intersection(validated_ttps_set)); fp = len(validated_ttps_set - article_ttps_set) + missing_in_mapping_count; fn = len(article_ttps_set - validated_ttps_set); then micro-averaged as overall_precision = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fp) and overall_recall = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fn). SO THE RULE IS EXACT STRING EQUALITY OF TECHNIQUE IDS, VIA SET INTERSECTION. There is no substring matching, no parent-technique credit, no sub-technique credit and no partial credit anywhere in the executing path. CONSEQUENCE THAT IS DIRECTLY ASSERTABLE, because TTP_Mapping.csv verifiably contains sub-technique IDs (T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003 and T1548.004 were quoted verbatim from it this cycle): if the ground truth says T1548 and a model predicts T1548.002, that prediction is admitted by the mapping check, fails the intersection, and is counted as a FALSE POSITIVE while T1548 is simultaneously counted as a FALSE NEGATIVE. One arguably-correct answer at the wrong granularity is penalised TWICE. SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS ctr-0004 BUT A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The scorer's own docstring says, verbatim, 'If a TTP's description does not match the expected mapping, issue a warning and do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs. (Such TTPs will be treated as false positives.)', and the directory README says the same in its own words -- 'Filtering: Only TTPs with matching descriptions are included' and, for a worked mismatch example, 'Result: Rejected (counted as false positive)'. THE CODE DOES THE OPPOSITE. On a description mismatch the live else-branch prints a warning and then executes corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id] followed by validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details -- it OVERWRITES the model's description with the canonical one and KEEPS the entry. There is no dead string literal here; the live code simply contradicts the docstring sitting above it in the same function. THE OPERATIVE CONSEQUENCE: the description check is INERT for scoring. A predicted technique ID counts on the sole condition that the ID appears in the mapping file, whatever the model wrote about it. So the scorer measures ID SELECTION ONLY, and any claim that it also measures whether the model correctly characterised the technique is false. THIRD FINDING, LENIENCY IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, RECORDED SO THE BIAS IS NOT ASSUMED TO RUN ONE WAY: a per-article json5 parse failure executes 'continue' and the whole surrounding block is wrapped in a bare 'except Exception', so an article whose model output is malformed is DROPPED ENTIRELY -- contributing no false negatives for its ground truth and no false positives. === PROMOTED TO SUPPORTED AT CYCLE 101 (T3). THE TWO SOURCES THAT CARRY IT ARE src-0038 AND src-0039, ADDED THIS CYCLE, AND THE PROMOTION ALSO RESTS ON A LOGICAL POINT CYCLE 100 DID NOT MAKE. ===
Cycle 100 set the bar at 'either the denominator or an independent replication'. Cycle 101 obtained a DENOMINATOR, though NOT the one that was being asked for, and the promotion turns on what that denominator shows.
(1) GPTZERO DOES PUBLISH A DENOMINATOR WHEN IT RUNS A SWEEP. src-0038 states, verbatim, that GPTZero 'used their automated Hallucination Check tool to scan 4,841 (of the 5290 papers accepted) papers from NeurIPS 2025' and found '100 hallucinated citations spanning 53 distinct papers (representing 1% of all accepted papers)'. THE CONSULTING SERIES' SILENCE IS THEREFORE NOT A VENDOR-WIDE INABILITY OR POLICY. It marks the consulting series as a DIFFERENT ARTEFACT CLASS from the academic sweep: a case-study series, released one instalment at a time by the vendor's own stated design, and not a sweep report.
(2) src-0039 SHOWS WHAT A PREVALENCE CLAIM REQUIRES, AND THE SERIES HAS NONE OF IT. An independent six-author audit of '111 million references across 2.5 million papers' publishes a corpus, a denominator, a verification method and per-corpus rates with an as-of date ('0.39% (arXiv), 0.21% (bioRxiv), 1.91% (SSRN), and 0.27% (PMC) as of August 2025'). The GPTZero consulting series publishes none of the four. The contrast is now CONCRETE rather than rhetorical.
(3) THE PwC INSTALMENT'S WITHHOLDING IS NOW TWO-FORM. Cycle 101 pair-rendered src-0037 on the r.jina.ai proxy and asked directly for the number of PwC reports scanned and for the selection method; the proxy returned ABSENT for both, matching cycle 99's direct render. Per the ctr-0049 rule that an absence needs a second form BEFORE it is filed, this absence is now properly established rather than provisional.
THE LOGICAL POINT, AND IT IS WHAT LETS THIS BE PROMOTED WITHOUT SETTLING THE MOTIVE QUESTION. The benign explanation written into this candidate at cycle 100 -- 'a vendor publishing case studies has no obligation to publish a sweep denominator, and the absence of one is not evidence of adverse selection' -- is now CORROBORATED rather than merely available, because (1) shows the vendor publishing denominators where it has them. BUT THAT EXPLANATION IS COMPATIBLE WITH THIS CANDIDATE RATHER THAN A DEFEATER OF IT. A case-study series cannot support a prevalence claim WHATEVER THE PUBLISHER'S MOTIVES. This candidate asserts an EVIDENTIAL LIMIT, not an accusation of adverse selection, and cycle 100 filed it under the shadow of a suspicion it did not actually need. THE SUSPICION IS SEVERABLE AND HAS BEEN SEVERED: the adverse-selection question stays OPEN at open_questions[2], at new open_questions[5] and at new candidate_resolutions[2], and NOTHING in this promotion prejudges it.
STRONG-CLAIM RULE SATISFIED: src-0038 and src-0039 share no author, no institution, no corpus and no funder, and neither was collected from the other's citations.

WITHIN LANCE, THE REGEX STAGE AND THE LLM STAGE DIVIDE RECALL FROM PRECISION, AND THE SCAFFOLDING'S CONTRIBUTION IS TO REDEFINE THE TASK RATHER THAN TO ADD PERFORMANCE ON TOP OF THE LLM. Verbatim, two-form identical across the direct and r.jina.ai renders of arxiv.org/html/2506.11325v2 (cycle 131): 'For each segment, we provide the LLM with the segment text along with a list of all extracted indicators (of the target type) from that segment.' and 'We then prompt it to classify each indicator as IoC or nonIoC and provide a justification for its label.' The LLM is handed an ENUMERATED CANDIDATE LIST produced by the regex stage and asked to CLASSIFY it, so it can contribute NO RECALL; and the paper assigns recall to the regex stage: 'Regular expression-based tools are highly effective in achieving high recall for IoC extraction, but struggle with precision.' THREE CONSEQUENCES. (1) LANCE's headline gain over the labelling baselines it is compared against is attributable to the LABELLING stage, since the regex-produced candidate set is common to that comparison -- BUT THE SHARED-DENOMINATOR PREMISE IS AN INFERENCE AND NOT A QUOTATION. (3) IT SHARPENS ctr-0001'S SYSTEM CONFOUND RATHER THAN DISSOLVING IT: src-0007's models GENERATE indicators and are scored on what they emit, while LANCE's LLM FILTERS indicators that a regex already found. Eliminating one rival explanation is not the same as demonstrating a causal claim about scaffolding, and promoting on that basis would be exactly the over-reach this candidate was created to resist. It stays 'proposed'. CYCLE-35 DECISION ON ctr-0007's OPEN QUESTION, WHICH CYCLE 29 EXPLICITLY DECLINED TO ANSWER. The question put was: does large model-side variance under PURELY SYNTACTIC noise SUPPORT the scaffolding hypothesis (regex pre-filtering and whitelisting are indifferent to dead-code injection and control-flow flattening, so scaffolding is what buys robustness) or UNDERCUT it (the variance is model-side, i.e. the model is exactly what varies)? I DECIDE THAT IT CUTS BOTH WAYS, AND THE CANDIDATE STAYS 'proposed' -- but that is a decision with content, not a refusal to decide, because the two readings turn out to be about DIFFERENT PROPOSITIONS and both can be true at once. (1) THE UNDERCUTTING READING IS THE STRONGER OF THE TWO ON THIS EVIDENCE. Five models, one corpus, one task, NO scaffolding on any arm, and a spread running from 100% to roughly 35% at P4. If the model were not what sets reliability, that spread could not exist. Model identity is therefore a large variance component under unscaffolded conditions, which is a direct qualification of a hypothesis whose whole content is that reliability is set 'mainly by the scaffolding around the model rather than by the LLM itself'. (2) THE SUPPORTING READING IS REAL BUT IS A COUNTERFACTUAL, NOT A MEASUREMENT. It is true that a regex extractor would be indifferent to dead-code injection and structural obfuscation, since those transformations leave the indicator in plain text; so scaffolding WOULD plausibly have erased Cohere's degradation. But src-0008 RUNS NO SCAFFOLDED ARM, so this is an inference about an experiment nobody performed, and it must not be entered as evidence. (3) THE DECISIVE POINT, AND IT IS WHY NEITHER READING PROMOTES OR DEMOTES THE CANDIDATE: src-0008 CANNOT ADJUDICATE THIS HYPOTHESIS AT ALL. Its task is recovering a planted indicator from JavaScript SOURCE CODE under adversarial transformation; this candidate is about extracting indicators from NARRATIVE THREAT REPORTS. A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality, so src-0007's precision is not a strict-match figure and may not be commensurable with src-0003's F1 even once a recall number exists. The full test() function body was not transcribed, so the exact conditions under which each rule fires are unknown. Resolving this needs the remainder of eval_ioc.py read, and ideally src-0003's own matching rule read alongside it -- a cheap, well-specified, high-value next step that requires no new search.
- [6] NEW (cycle 35). THIS SUPERSEDES open_questions[5] ABOVE, WHICH IS LEFT IN PLACE PER THE APPEND-ONLY SPIRIT BUT IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. This discharges step (i) of ctr-0004, open since cycle 27. open_questions[5] says src-0017's evaluator matches 'with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions'. IT DOES NOT. The EXECUTING code in stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/eval/eval_ioc.py is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, verbatim: 'true_positives = sum(any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) for pred in pred_list)', with 'false_positives = len(pred_list) - true_positives' and 'false_negatives = sum(not any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for pred in pred_list) for gt in gt_set)'. The two-directional variant and the exact-match variant are EACH ENCLOSED IN A TRIPLE-QUOTED STRING LITERAL and never execute; the comment lines cycle 21 quoted are the headers standing above those dead blocks. THE SOURCE STATES THE SAME RULE IN ITS OWN PROSE -- IoC sub-README, verbatim: 'A prediction is considered a True Positive (TP) if pred.lower() in gt.lower() for any ground truth IOC from the same source'. Code and documentation agree with each other and against what this issue said. THE CONSEQUENCE IS AN ASYMMETRIC BIAS, NOT A ONE-WAY ONE. The rule is LENIENT toward short or fragmentary predictions, since any prediction that is a substring of a longer ground-truth entry scores TP. It is STRICT against verbose predictions, since a prediction containing the ground-truth IoC plus surrounding text scores a FALSE POSITIVE -- and that is the characteristic failure mode of a free-form LLM extractor, i.e. exactly the case the dead two-directional block would have scored TP. A verbose-but-correct prediction is moreover penalised TWICE, as a false positive AND as a false negative, because the ground-truth entry it contains is simultaneously left unmatched by the false_negatives line above. So the limitation recorded at src-0017.md, that 'A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality', is HALF RIGHT and must never be repeated unqualified: relative to strict equality this matcher INFLATES on one axis and DEFLATES on the other, and THE NET SIGN IS UNKNOWN because it is the difference of two unmeasured quantities. PARTIAL MITIGATION, recorded so the deflation is not over-read: both sides pass through the same normalisation chain (transcribed verbatim in ctr-0004), which strips defanging -- hxxp to http, bracket removal -- and truncates at the first ' - ' separator, so the commonest verbose-prediction artefacts in CTI text are normalised away BEFORE matching. What survives the chain as verbose FP is free prose around the indicator, and a URL-with-path predicted against a bare-domain ground truth. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN: the net sign and magnitude of the bias. It cannot be recovered without the per-model prediction files, which are now confirmed ABSENT from both release mirrors -- see open_questions[7].

The cycle-39 rewrite above retires the extraction-versus-generation calibration gradient, and its stated ground is that the gradient 'holds on ECE at every paradigm, vanishes on Brier at zero-shot, REVERSES on Brier at few-shot'. A proper score decomposes into calibration loss plus refinement loss -- src-0029 Section 3.1, re-confirmed verbatim at cycle 80 on the ar5iv render as 'E[d(S,Ydot)] = E[d(S,C)] + E[d(C,Ydot)]', the first term being calibration loss and the second refinement loss (mathematical notation transliterated to ASCII). A Brier difference between two task families is therefore the SUM of a calibration difference and a refinement difference. Two families can differ in calibration by any amount whatever and still post equal Brier scores, provided the refinement difference cancels it. SO THE BRIER MEANS FAILING TO REPRODUCE THE ECE ORDERING IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE CALIBRATION GRADIENT IS ABSENT. It is equally consistent with a real calibration gradient offset by a refinement gradient running the other way -- which is precisely the shape candidate_resolutions[7] and open_questions[9] independently isolate in the extraction attack-vector row. ECE AND THE BRIER SCORE ARE NOT TWO MEASURES OF ONE QUANTITY, AND src-0001's OWN METHODOLOGICAL ASSERTION THAT THEY ARE IS CONTRADICTED BY TWO INDEPENDENT PEER-REVIEWED METHODOLOGY SOURCES. READ THE SCOPE LIMIT IN THE LAST PARAGRAPH BEFORE USING THIS ANYWHERE. (1) THE QUOTATIONS, WHICH ARE THE EVIDENCE. src-0028 (Popordanoska, Gruber, Tiulpin, Buettner and Blaschko, AISTATS 2024, PMLR 238:3466-3474, peer-reviewed), abstract verbatim: 'Every proper score decomposes into two fundamental components -- proper calibration error and refinement -- utilizing a Bregman divergence.' src-0029 (Silva Filho, Song, Perello-Nieto, Santos-Rodriguez, Kull and Flach, Machine Learning 2023, DOI 10.1007/s10994-023-06336-7, peer-reviewed on arXiv's own Comments and Journal-reference fields), Section 3 verbatim: 'Both Brier score and log-loss are strictly proper scoring rules'; Section 3.1 verbatim: 'The decomposition of proper scoring rule phi into calibration loss and refinement loss is then the sum of expected loss between S and C and expected loss between C and Y'. src-0029 also records that the terminology has drifted, Section 3.1 verbatim: 'Validity, later known as reliability (Murphy and Winkler, 1977), is now often called calibration loss (Kull and Flach, 2015)...Sharpness, which is now commonly called refinement loss and was also known as resolution (Murphy and Winkler, 1977)' -- which is part of why the two quantities get conflated in the first place. (2) THE INFERENCE, LABELLED AS AN INFERENCE AND NOT AS A QUOTATION. Neither source names ECE. The step from 'a proper score decomposes into calibration plus refinement' to 'the Brier score is not interchangeable with a calibration error' requires the premise that the Brier score IS a proper score, which src-0029 states verbatim, and the premise that ECE estimates a calibration error, which is what ECE is by construction. Cycle 78 drew this inference and cycle 79 endorses it, but it is DERIVED and a successor must not quote it as either source's words. (3) WHAT IT CONTRADICTS. src-0001 asserts verbatim: 'The ECE and BS, are two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration.' On src-0028 and src-0029 that sentence is WRONG AS STATED -- the Brier score confounds calibration with refinement, so two systems with identical calibration error can carry different Brier scores. THE CONFLICT IS FILED AS ctr-0039 PER HARD RULE 3 AND IS NOT DECIDED HERE; this candidate states the methodological position and the contradiction entry records the conflict and its repair path. (4) WHY THIS MATTERS TO THIS ISSUE RATHER THAN BEING A FOOTNOTE. open_questions[6] -- nine cycles old, twice narrowed, and the question a T3 on two DOWNSTREAM issues is told to read before citing src-0001 -- was built entirely on the premise that the two metrics measure one thing and therefore ought to agree. If they do not measure one thing, the Table 6 divergence is EXPECTED behaviour and not an anomaly. THIS DOES NOT DISPLACE CYCLE 75's ONE-ROW-ARTEFACT FINDING AND THE TWO ARE COMPATIBLE: cycle 75 showed WHERE the divergence comes from (a single outlier row), and this shows WHY such a row is possible at all. open_questions[9] asks whether the two explanations are in fact the same explanation, and CYCLE 79 DOES NOT ASSERT THAT THEY ARE. (5) A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONSEQUENCE THAT IS NEW TO THIS BASE AND CUTS AGAINST src-0001's ECE COLUMN RATHER THAN ITS BRIER COLUMN. Both sources impeach the binned ECE estimator. src-0028 verbatim: 'using a fixed binning scheme represents a lower bound of the respective calibration error'; 'the number of bins and the binning scheme can significantly influence the estimated value'; 'there is no optimal default since every setting has a different bias-variance tradeoff'. src-0029 Section 4.1 verbatim: 'Even perfectly calibrated scores may result in a visually non-calibrated reliability diagram with a deviation of up to half the bin width from the diagonal'. src-0001 states no bin count and no binning scheme anywhere this base has read, so every src-0001 ECE figure is a point estimate from an unstated estimator with a known lower-bound bias. (6) WHAT NEITHER SOURCE SUPPLIES, AND THE NEGATIVE IS PART OF THE CLAIM. NEITHER RANKS THE TWO METRICS. src-0028's full text returned ABSENT to a direct question about ranking them -- ONE-FORM ABSENT, not a two-render confirmed absence -- and src-0029 says only 'It is good practice to use them together with the proper scoring rules presented in Section 3, to get a full evaluation'. (7) SCOPE LIMIT, BINDING, AND THE REASON THIS CANDIDATE IS AT RISK OF MISUSE. src-0028 AND src-0029 MEASURE NO LLM AND NO SECURITY TASK. They are METHODOLOGY. REPEAT-RUN INCONSISTENCY IS A PROPERTY OF THE INSTRUMENT AND NOT A CONFIGURATION ERROR, AND SETTING TEMPERATURE TO ZERO DOES NOT REMOVE IT FOR API-SERVED MODELS. STATUS IS 'proposed' AND THE REASON IS IN THE LAST PARAGRAPH. (1) THE CLAIM AND ITS EVIDENCE. src-0030 (Coqueret et al., arXiv 2607.24372) names FOUR mechanisms, Section 3 headings verbatim: '3.1 Deliberate sampling', '3.2 Silent model updates', '3.3 Floating point rounding', '3.4 Expert routing'. Verbatim: 'Setting T=0 removes deliberate sampling but...does not eliminate all sources of randomness in frontier models served through online APIs.' Abstract verbatim: 'Exact reproduction is therefore generally not possible when using proprietary application programming interfaces.' It demonstrates the point on its own runs, Section 4.2 and Figure 3 verbatim: locally, 'the distribution of statistics based on Gemma-4 deployed locally...is entirely concentrated at a single value under T=0'; via API at T=0, 'the distribution becomes much more concentrated but does not collapse to a single value. Instead, the estimates take only four distinct values (with one occurring only rarely).' Its normative conclusion, abstract verbatim: 'LLM outputs should be treated as draws from a distribution rather than as fixed measurements.' (2) WHY THIS IS STRUCTURALLY IMPORTANT TO THIS ISSUE AND NOT MERELY BACKGROUND. EVERY consistency measurement in this base -- src-0001's CI widths, src-0016's five-run recurrence counts, src-0018's cross-run decision consistency, src-0031's 400 runs -- rests on the unstated assumption that repeat-run variation is a real property of the system under test rather than an artefact of a configuration the experimenter could have fixed. UNTIL CYCLE 78 THIS BASE HAD NO CITATION FOR THAT ASSUMPTION. src-0030 supplies one, and it also supplies the boundary: the assumption is safe for API-served models and NOT safe as a general claim about LLMs, because locally deployed models at T=0 DO collapse to a single value. So the consistency half of this issue is a claim about DEPLOYED CTI SYSTEMS SERVED THROUGH APIS, which is what the CTI sources actually measure, and it should be stated that way rather than as a claim about language models as such. THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHICH METRIC SHOULD GOVERN A CALIBRATION CLAIM ON CTI, AND WHY. The paper does not distinguish them, offers no reliability diagram, and never comments on the divergence; this base has no source that discusses ECE-versus-Brier behaviour at all. An answer needs either a methodological source on proper scoring rules versus binned calibration error, or a CTI source reporting both metrics with a stated preference. UNTIL THEN, NO CYCLE MAY STATE AN EXTRACTION-VERSUS-GENERATION CALIBRATION GRADIENT WITHOUT NAMING THE METRIC IT HOLDS ON, and the only paradigm at which it holds on BOTH metrics is fine-tuning. This question said flatly that this base 'has no source that discusses ECE-versus-Brier behaviour at all'. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE. src-0013's Table I prints ECE and Brier SIDE BY SIDE, per model, per temperature, under FOUR elicitation methods, and cycle 62 pulled two of those blocks. WHAT THE COMPARISON SHOWS: IN src-0013 THE TWO METRICS DO NOT DIVERGE. Within the Verbalized block the model ordering is identical on both -- by ECE, Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.25-0.26 < Qwen3-Coder-Next 0.41-0.42 < GPT-4o-mini 0.46-0.48; by Brier, Gemini 0.26 < Qwen 0.36-0.38 < GPT-4o-mini 0.37-0.39 -- and within the Token Probability block both metrics agree that calibration is uniformly bad (ECE 0.79-0.81, Brier 0.74-0.80) and agree on the direction of the small GPT-versus-Gemini difference. - **Supported:** REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 28 (T3), executing step (i) of ctr-0002's resolution path. THE 86-VS-52 FRAMING IS RETIRED, NOT REPAIRED. The old text of this candidate said 'every one of the 5 tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate substantially exceeds its correct attribution rate (e.g. GPT-4-turbo: 86% plausible vs 52% correct; Gemini-1.5: 74% vs 38%)'; CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it CONTAINS Correct Accuracy and that inequality is true by construction for every model on every dataset. It evidenced nothing and is withdrawn. WHAT REPLACES IT. CTI-TAA partitions each response into three buckets, verbatim: 'correct answer (when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases), plausible answer (when the threat report lacks sufficient details to pinpoint the answer, but the LLM provides a plausible or related threat actor within a similar group), and incorrect answer (when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation)'. The THIRD bucket is the paper's own hallucination-inclusive misattribution rate and equals 100 minus Plausible Accuracy: GPT-4-turbo 14%, GPT-3.5-turbo 38%, Gemini-1.5 26%, LLAMA3-70B 20%, LLAMA3-8B 64%, over 50 real threat reports, with the authors stating that they 'manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use'. THOSE FIVE VALUES ARE DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1 BY THIS AGENT AND ARE NOT PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER; every cell they are derived from was re-verified EXACT against Table 1 by two independent fetches at cycle 23, and the ChatGPT-4 row was re-confirmed a third time at cycle 28. THE FINDING: outright misattribution of the threat actor is common in 2024-era models, from roughly one report in seven for the best model to nearly two in three for the weakest, on real reports scored with alias tolerance. WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM, and the distinction is the whole point of this issue: src-0002 measures WRONGNESS, NOT CONFIDENCE. It records no verbalised confidence, no hedging rate, no calibration metric and no reader-facing plausibility judgement, and no sentence in the paper interprets the correct-versus-plausible gap. Its 'plausible' bucket is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor from a similar group -- arguably reasonable behaviour under ambiguity -- and is explicitly NOT its hallucination bucket. The string 'plausible-sounding' does not occur in the paper, though this state presented it in scare quotes for 27 cycles. This candidate is therefore supported as an ATTRIBUTION-ERROR-RATE finding and supplies no support whatever for the 'confident' half of this issue's title. src-0004 has been REMOVED from this candidate's evidence: see open_question[2], answered this cycle, which finds the ENISA error to be a distinct sub-type invisible to CTI-TAA's scoring rule. Under CTI-TAA's own rule the ENISA sentence would be scored CORRECT. It names two taxonomies and gives verbatim tag examples 'estimative-language:likelihood-probability="almost-no-chance"' and 'estimative-language:confidence-in-analytic-judgment="moderate"', alongside 'admiralty-scale:source-reliability="a/b/c..."'. LIKELIHOOD-PROBABILITY grades how likely the claim is to be true; CONFIDENCE-IN-ANALYTIC-JUDGMENT grades confidence in the judgement itself, i.e. in the sufficiency of the evidence and reasoning -- and the two are tagged separately and can move independently. THE SECOND AXIS IS PRECISELY THE QUANTITY open_questions[3] DERIVED, UNDER AN OPERATIONAL NAME. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART: the objection that attribution confidence is too ill-posed to measure because the ground truth is contested DOES NOT HOLD. A well-posed evaluation is constructible today -- elicit both axes on an attribution task and test whether confidence-in-analytic-judgment tracks evidential determinacy while likelihood tracks correctness -- and CTIBench's own correct/plausible/incorrect partition, whose 'plausible' bucket is scoped by src-0002's verbatim definition to reports that LACK SUFFICIENT DETAIL to pinpoint the answer, already supplies a determinacy label to test against. THIS IS A DESIGN CLAIM, NOT A MEASUREMENT. src-0024 contains no LLM, no model and no number, and may never be cited as evidence about model behaviour. - A DESIGN QUESTION THIS ISSUE SHOULD NOT DUCK, because it determines whether the issue is answerable in principle: WHAT WOULD THE RIGHT MEASUREMENT EVEN LOOK LIKE? Attribution is unlike the tasks calibration is normally measured on, because the ground truth is itself contested, aliased and sometimes genuinely underdetermined by the report -- which is precisely why CTIBench needed a 'plausible' bucket and why it scores an ALIAS as correct. A confidence measurement that ignored that would be measuring the wrong thing. So a well-posed target is narrower than 'is the model calibrated': it is whether a model's expressed confidence DISCRIMINATES between reports whose attribution is determined by the evidence and reports whose attribution is not. If no published work measures that, saying so with this reasoning attached is a legitimate resolution of this issue and should be recorded as such rather than treated as a failure to find an answer.

STATUS IS 'proposed', NOT 'supported', AND THE REASON IS STATED FIRST: this is ONE source making a STRONG claim, and this base's T3 rule requires two independent sources before a strong claim is promoted. THE PROPOSED RESOLUTION: task-dependence in CTI is partly a property of the TASK'S GROUND TRUTH rather than of the model, and that is a mechanism the scoring-rule objection (ctr-0009) does not touch. THE EVIDENCE. src-0043 trains a multi-label classifier to map CVE free-text descriptions to MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques on a curated gold set of 1,207 expert CTID mappings, and then tests whether LLM-generated labels can extend it. Verbatim from the abstract, CONFIRMED ON BOTH RENDERS: 'LLM-generated labels, with approximately 0.39 agreement with expert annotations, provide no reliable improvement at any expansion size and reduce rare-technique coverage at around 1,000 added CVEs', and 'additional expert-curated data consistently improves performance, whereas LLM-labeled data does not, indicating that the classifier is limited by label quality rather than dataset size'. WHY THIS BEARS ON THIS ISSUE AND NOT MERELY ON ttp-attack-mapping-reliability: it supplies a NON-ARTEFACTUAL mechanism for why a reasoning-heavy sub-task should measure worse than a mechanical one. The authors state (BODY RENDER ONLY) that 'Mapping a CVE to ATT&CK is genuinely hard and partly subjective' and that classifier and LLM reach similar agreement against gold (~0.39-0.41), which they read as an inherent task ceiling rather than a modelling failure. If a sub-task's ground truth is itself partly subjective and its expert mappings are, in the authors' words, 'not automatically exhaustive', then low measured reliability on that sub-task is not fully attributable to the model and not fully explained away by a strict matching rule either -- the task is differently hard in a way that survives both. THREE OBJECTIONS PRICED, NOT WAVED THROUGH. (1) KC4 IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A MEASUREMENT: 0.39 and 0.41 are MODEL-versus-GOLD agreements and NO human-versus-human inter-annotator figure appears on either render, so the ceiling is the authors' interpretation of two model-vs-gold numbers. This is the single largest weakness of this candidate and it is why the status is 'proposed'. (2) MODALITY GAP: src-0043 maps from CVE DESCRIPTIONS, whereas every other ATT&CK measurement in this base maps from threat reports or narrative CTI text; a ceiling on the CVE-description task does not automatically transfer to the report task. (3) THE NULL IS SCOPED BY THE AUTHORS to labels AT ~0.39 AGREEMENT, one model family and one prompt configuration -- a better labeler is not tested and is not ruled out. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: src-0043 measures no mechanical-extraction sub-task, so it offers NO within-study extraction-versus-reasoning contrast of its own and is NOT evidence about the ordinal axis, which the cycle-16 split moved out of this issue. Note also that src-0043's KC3 is a general warning this issue should carry: checkpoint selection on a small test split produced recall@5 differences of up to 0.05 between otherwise identical runs, so a single-run cross-sub-task gap of that order is within this study's own noise floor. A CITATION HOLD APPLIES to src-0043's macro-F1 decrement, which the two renders report as 0.04 and 0.026; only the direction and the null verdict are citable. [src-0043]

Its Table VI gives a WITHIN-STUDY CROSS-SUB-TASK contrast between non-targeted detection (VD) and targeted detection given a CWE hint (TVD), on the PBD split, CONFIRMED ON BOTH RENDERS for two models: CodeLlama VD 75.9 / TVD 92.3 with Patch Verification PV 21.2 / TPV 11.2, and DeepSeek-R1 VD 96.1 / TVD 98.7 with PV 4.5 / TPV 0.7. NOTE WHAT THAT PATTERN IS: giving the model the sub-task hint RAISES accuracy on vulnerable samples and LOWERS it on patched ones, in both models, which is a THRESHOLD MOVE, not a competence gain. THE TRANSFERABLE POINT FOR THIS ISSUE: a sub-task whose prompt or framing shifts a model's answer bias will show a large apparent accuracy gap against a sub-task that does not, at unchanged underlying competence. TWO SUB-TASKS MOVING INDEPENDENTLY UNDER A COMMON INTERVENTION IS DIRECT WITHIN-STUDY EVIDENCE THAT RELIABILITY IS NOT ONE UNIFORM PROPERTY -- which is exactly this issue's narrow claim, on a within-study design, holding team, corpus and harness constant. A FURTHER CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING THIS CANDIDATE WAS QUEUED UNDER: cycle 124's queue entry described src-0042's central finding as 'task-dependent direction instability -- fine-tuning helping on one task and hurting on another within one study design'. THE CLAIM: the proposed ordinal axis 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' is NOT supported by the only commensurable cross-sub-task measurement available in this base, and the extraction-versus-reasoning binary is too coarse to explain where CTI reliability breaks down. TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES, from two unaffiliated teams on two corpora with two disjoint model sets. (1) src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows -- one corpus, one 15-model set, one metric -- gives a Contextualization stage mean of 0.636 (IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607) against an Attribution stage mean of 0.602 (TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511). The 0.034 gap is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best task in the subset is an Attribution-stage task. (2) src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models: GPT-4o's attribution rubric of 1.140/5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 against a derived TTP F1 of 0.2502 (at or below), while o3-mini's 2.968/5 normalises to 0.594 or 0.492 against 0.2337 (above), under both defensible normalisations. THREE MATERIAL CAVEATS. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose columns in printed order, a pattern of unknown cause verified as-printed by three pulls across two URL forms; dropping all four leaves 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) The fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so this candidate refutes the extraction-versus-classification-versus-attribution part of the ordering and is SILENT on generation, which remains supported in the parent issue by src-0001's extraction-versus-generation confidence-interval-width split of 0.02 against 0.06. - **Supported:** CREATED cycle 16 by T2, discharging carry-forward [3] and merging carry-forward [15]; six cycles elapsed between the first proposal of this issue and the first cycle with standing to create it. Two independent sources -- different teams, different task framings, different model generations, different years -- find the same failure: the decision threshold is set so permissively that the system accepts or acts on most of what a human analyst would reject. src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026) measures automated triage on a real company's daily CTI workflow and reports an extreme asymmetry, recall (Accepted) 0.90-1.00 against precision (Accepted) 0.27-0.40 across all four models tested. src-0015 (OpenSec, Jan 2026) measures frontier incident-response agents over 40 episodes per model and finds GPT-5.2 containing in 100% of episodes at an 82.5% false-positive rate, DeepSeek 3.2 92.5% at 65%, Gemini 3 75% at 57.5%, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 62.5% at 45%, with an evidence-gated action rate of only 0.375-0.542 -- every model acts without first fetching trusted evidence about the target entity on a majority or near-majority of its containment actions. WHY THIS IS AN ISSUE AND NOT A FOOTNOTE UNDER ACCURACY: src-0015 locates the defect precisely, stating that 'All models correctly identify the ground-truth threat when they act; the calibration gap is not in detection but in restraint.' Detection accuracy is fine. These systems would be scored WELL by essentially every metric used elsewhere in this knowledge base, and the defect is invisible to all of them -- which is exactly the argument for giving it its own issue rather than filing it under an existing accuracy-shaped one. PROVENANCE ASYMMETRY, do not flatten it: src-0007 is institutionally affiliated, methodologically detailed, and had all nine of its stored Table 4 rows re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 exact to four decimal places; src-0015 is by its own recorded assessment the weakest-provenance source in this base -- single-author preprint filed cs.AI, no stated venue, peer review or affiliation, n=40 synthetic RL-seed episodes per model with no confidence intervals, and only the GPT-5.2-versus-Sonnet-4.5 contrast robust, with the middle two models' ordering unresolved. The claim therefore RESTS on src-0007; src-0015 corroborates its direction on a different task and a newer model generation, which is worth a great deal for showing the failure is not one benchmark's artefact, and is worth little as independent quantification. ONE POOLING ERROR TO AVOID: src-0015's 'calibration' is an action-threshold construct (false-positive rate, evidence-gating), NOT the ECE/Brier confidence calibration of src-0001 and src-0013, and the two must never be averaged or quoted as the same measurement. [src-0007], [src-0015]
- Proposed (unconfirmed): PROPOSED, ENTERED CYCLE 135 (T2) FROM src-0047. THIS IS THE FIRST CANDIDATE ADDED TO THIS ISSUE SINCE ITS CREATION AT CYCLE 16, AND IT IS ENTERED BY A T2 THAT WAS TARGETED AT A DIFFERENT ISSUE, BECAUSE THE SELECTOR HAS NEVER ONCE REACHED THIS ONE -- attempts is EMPTY after 134 cycles, the only such issue in the graph. See ctr-0067 and the standing honesty item on the T5 tie-break list. THE CLAIM, AND IT COMES AT THIS ISSUE FROM THE OPPOSITE SIDE TO candidate_resolutions[0]. This issue asks whether LLM triage systems fail by ACCEPTING OR ACTING ON FAR TOO MUCH, an under-refusal failure that accuracy-based evaluation does not detect. src-0047 supplies a deployed-system datum about THE INSTRUMENT THAT IS SUPPOSED TO PREVENT EXACTLY THAT: the confidence gate at the high-confidence operating point that governs automated triage. Verbatim from the abstract, captured on two renders and matching word for word: 'We further show that the trained calibrator is necessary - an untrained confidence judge collapses high-confidence recall to zero - and that a finetuned 30B model significantly outperforms frontier general-purpose models, motivating targeted training over scale.' And, on how the gate came to be damaged: 'We find that CoT reasoning also degrades the label-token probabilities that automated triage relies on, so we separately train a calibrator that reads the full reasoning trace and estimates the probability that the verdict is correct.' WHY THIS BEARS ON THIS ISSUE AND NOT ONLY ON CALIBRATION GENERALLY. An under-refusal failure is a failure of the ABSTENTION-OR-ESCALATION BOUNDARY, and in this system that boundary IS a confidence threshold. src-0047 reports that the threshold instrument is DAMAGED BY THE SAME TRAINING THAT IMPROVES ACCURACY, and that operating it untrained yields nothing usable at the automation point. THAT IS A MECHANISM BY WHICH AN ACCURACY-EVALUATED TRIAGE SYSTEM CAN LOOK FINE AND STILL MIS-SET WHAT IT ACTS ON. IT DOES NOT MEASURE OVER-ACCEPTANCE, AND IT IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THIS PARTICULAR SYSTEM UNDER-REFUSED. HOLDS, IDENTICAL TO THOSE RECORDED ON consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode's candidate for this source AND EQUALLY BINDING HERE. NO calibration metric of any kind (ABSENT, asked directly) -- direction only, never magnitude. DO NOT ATTACH A NUMBER TO 'ZERO' BEYOND THE WORD ITSELF and do not name an operating point; cycle 134 did not locate the supporting table. 82.6%, 43.0% AND 18.3% ARE UNDER A CITATION HOLD -- no cycle has seen the table behind them, and the two recall figures are RELATIVE improvements over 'a direct-label LLM classifier', never absolute recalls. NO ABSTENTION OR REFUSAL RATE IS REPORTED, so this source measures no refusal behaviour directly. NO repeat-query consistency and no run-to-run variance (ABSENT). The task is SOC alert triage of Windows endpoint detections, and MITRE ATT&CK mappings are an INPUT FEATURE rather than a prediction target. Vendor-authored on proprietary telemetry and NOT independently reproducible; NOT peer-reviewed; single deployment, single OS, single vendor pipeline. CoT training and RL-with-verifiable-rewards are applied jointly and were not ablated. WHY status IS proposed AND NOT supported: one preprint, vendor-authored, with no calibration and no refusal metric, and -- THE DECISIVE REASON -- NO CYCLE HAS YET READ THIS SOURCE'S BODY FOR THIS ISSUE. Cycle 134 read it against a different issue's questions, and cycle 135 entered it here without spending a fetch. A T3 ON THIS ISSUE SHOULD READ src-0047 END TO END AND SHOULD LOOK SPECIFICALLY FOR THE TABLE BEHIND THE HIGH-CONFIDENCE-RECALL CLAIM AND FOR ANY REPORTED ESCALATION OR DEFERRAL RATE. **Open questions:**
- IS OVER-ACCEPTANCE A PROPERTY OF THE MODELS OR OF THE HARNESS? This is the issue's central unknown and neither source addresses it. Neither src-0007 nor src-0015 varies the decision threshold, the stated cost of a false positive in the prompt, the availability of an explicit abstain option, or the presence of a human confirmation step. src-0003 established for a different sub-task (IoC extraction) that scaffolding around the model can dominate measured reliability; the analogous experiment for triage -- does an explicit abstain option, a stated false-positive cost, or a required evidence-fetch step move precision (Accepted) off 0.27-0.40 -- has not been run by any source in this base. Until it is, 'the models under-refuse' and 'these harnesses were built with no refusal affordance' are indistinguishable.
- WHAT IS THE OPERATIONAL COST, and is it actually worse than the status quo? Neither source converts its false-positive rate into analyst hours, containment blast radius, or alert-fatigue effects, so precision (Accepted) of 0.27 cannot yet be compared against human triage on any common currency. Note a structural obstacle: src-0007's ground truth IS the human analyst's accept/reject decision, so by construction it carries no human error bar and cannot tell us whether human triage would score better on its own benchmark.
- MERGED IN FROM carry-forward [15] at the cycle-16 split decision; cycle 12 excluded this from the knowledge base as a source and cycle 16 judges it belongs HERE, as an open question rather than as evidence. The mirror image of automated over-acceptance is AI-generated security claims arriving INBOUND in volume: curl ended its HackerOne bug bounty on 31 January 2026 after a flood of AI-generated 'slop' vulnerability reports, with reported figures of roughly 20% of submissions being AI slop by mid-2025 and the confirmed-vulnerability rate falling from about 15% historically to under 5%. 'AI slop arrives inbound AND automated triage cannot filter it' is a coherent single problem that this issue and carry-forward [15] describe better jointly than either does alone -- and it has a sharp practical edge, because if automated triage accepts 60-73% of what human analysts reject, it is precisely the wrong instrument for the volume problem it is most often proposed to solve. THIS IS NOT YET EVIDENCE AND MUST NOT BE CITED AS SUCH: no curl/HackerOne source exists in state/knowledge/index.json and a T2 must not invent sources (G1). A future T1 should collect it, reported at bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/curl-ending-bug-bounty-program-after-flood-of-ai-slop-reports/. Until collected, this is a question, not a claim.
- Does the under-refusal generalise to the CTI sub-tasks measured elsewhere in this base? If a model were asked to extract IoCs or map ATT&CK techniques with an explicit 'insufficient evidence' option available, would it use it? src-0014 supplies this base's only abstention data -- self-consistency collapsing coverage to 24.04-60.85% -- but on vulnerability detection rather than CTI, and it measures abstention INDUCED by sampling disagreement rather than abstention OFFERED as a choice, so it does not answer this.
- Is there a trade-off frontier, or is this simply a badly-set threshold? src-0007's recall (Accepted) of 0.90-1.00 alongside precision of 0.27-0.40 is consistent with a threshold set to maximise recall; nobody has published the precision the same models reach at a recall of, say, 0.7. If the frontier is favourable, this is a tuning problem and largely solved; if precision stays low across the whole frontier, it is a capability problem. No source in this base reports a precision-recall curve for triage.

## Unresolved contradictions

- (task-dependent-reliability-framing) ONE ISSUE ASSERTS AS SUPPORTED EXACTLY WHAT ANOTHER ISSUE HAS FORMALLY WITHDRAWN, ON THE SAME TABLE AND THE SAME NUMBERS. Opened by the cycle-33 T4 while pricing carry-forward [47](d) and [34]. This is a conflict between two SUPPORTED claims inside this state, which is precisely G3's test, and it is filed nowhere else: ctr-0008 covers only the 1.140-versus-3.612 half and is filed against a DIFFERENT issue_id, and ctr-0004 is filed against ioc-extraction-reliability. NO contradiction entry has ever been filed against task-dependent-reliability-framing. THE CLAIM IN CONFLICT, verbatim from this issue's SECOND candidate_resolution (status 'supported', evidence [src-0007, src-0013], added cycle 16 by T2): 'Two further within-study measurements strengthen the NARROW claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- and both are of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task. (1) src-0007: on one expert-annotated corpus drawn from a real company's CTI workflow, the same four models reach IoC-extraction precision 0.8240-0.8846 while scoring 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o) and 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini) precision/recall on MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification, and GPT-4o scores 1.140 out of 5 on the threat-actor Attribution rubric against 3.612 out of 5 for root-cause content in the same table -- roughly a 3x spread across sub-tasks with everything else held constant.' BOTH OF ITS TWO src-0007 COMPARISONS ARE NOW KNOWN TO BE NON-COMMENSURABLE, EACH REFUTED BY A SUPPORTED CANDIDATE ELSEWHERE IN THIS GRAPH, AND ITS STATED METHODOLOGICAL WARRANT IS FALSE. CONFLICT 1 -- THE IoC-VERSUS-TTP SPREAD. ttp-attack-mapping-reliability's candidate 2 carries a cycle-31 addendum headed 'CLAIM (b) IS NOW WITHDRAWN' which withdraws THIS EXACT INFERENCE in this exact form: 'The argument was that because the identical models on the identical corpus through the identical harness reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. That inference silently assumed the two numbers were produced by comparable scoring. THEY ARE NOT.' The two rules are now BOTH known from executing code in one artefact (src-0017): the IoC side is ONE-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT, any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) (ctr-0004, cycle 27), and the ATT&CK side is EXACT TECHNIQUE-ID SET INTERSECTION with no substring, parent, sub-technique or partial credit (ttp candidate 3, read cycle 31 and REPLICATED cycle 32 with ten verbatim string checks, plus the finding that TTP_Mapping.csv carries a 'sub-technique of' parent column WHICH THE LOADER DISCARDS, so a T1548.002 prediction against a T1548 ground truth is counted as a false positive AND a false negative simultaneously). THE DECISIVE POINT, AND IT IS NEW HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED: THE DIRECTION OF THE SCORING BIAS IS THE DIRECTION OF THE REPORTED FINDING. The leniently-scored task is the one that scores high and the strictly-scored task is the one that scores low. So the 3x spread this candidate presents as a sub-task difficulty fact is exactly what these two scoring rules would manufacture from equal underlying performance. The confound is no longer merely possible and unquantified; its SIGN is known and it aligns with the claim. CONFLICT 2 -- THE 1.140-VERSUS-3.612 RUBRIC CONTRAST. Per ctr-0008 (cycle 30, confirmed by two fetches of the paper's Appendix C.2 on two URL renderings and again at cycle 31 from the live sys_prompt string in eval/root_cause.py retrieved whole), the dimension named 'Attribution' IS DEFINED DIFFERENTLY IN THE TWO RUBRIC BLOCKS: in the Threat Actor block it measures SOURCE LINKING ('5: Fully attributable; all details are clearly linked to the original article'), and no anchor in that block mentions identifying a threat actor; in the Root Cause block it measures THREAT-ACTOR IDENTIFICATION ('5: Perfect attribution; accurately identifies the threat actor, their objectives, and the precise relationship to the incident's root cause'). 1.140 and 3.612 are two different constructs sharing one column name, and the labels run OPPOSITE to the way this candidate reads them. WHY THIS IS FILED AGAINST THIS ISSUE AND NOT LEFT TO ctr-0008. ctr-0008 flags this issue in passing as having 'the LARGEST SCORING EXPOSURE' but is filed against attribution-confident-wrong-gap, so per-issue queries over open contradictions do not surface it here, and it does not address conflict 1 at all. Conflict 1 is unfiled anywhere against this issue. THE FALSE WARRANT, WHICH IS THE MOST TRANSFERABLE PART. The candidate's own justification for treating these as strong evidence is that they are 'of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task'. That is carry-forward [34] stated as a virtue and it is false: A WITHIN-STUDY DESIGN DOES NOT HOLD THE SCORING RULE CONSTANT, and both of this candidate's within-study comparisons are now demonstrated instances of the rule varying with the sub-task. There are now SEVEN documented non-commensurable instances in this base (src-0017/ctr-0004; src-0003's classification-over-a-regex-candidate-set; src-0005's all-or-nothing multi-select; src-0002/ctr-0006's Micro-versus-Macro-F1 with no stated ATT&CK correctness rule; src-0007's rubric against itself per ctr-0008; src-0007's IoC rule against its own ATT&CK rule; and src-0008's body text against its own Table 6 caption). WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY DEFINES. Appendix C.2 prints SEPARATE criteria blocks for Threat Actor content and Root Cause content, and the dimension named 'Attribution' IS DEFINED DIFFERENTLY IN THE TWO BLOCKS. Verbatim, THREAT ACTOR block, all five anchors: 'Attribution: 1: Information is unverified or unattributed. 2: Major attribution issues; many details are not clearly linked. 3: Moderately attributable; some details lack clear source references. 4: Mostly attributable; minor gaps in linking information. 5: Fully attributable; all details are clearly linked to the original article.' Verbatim, ROOT CAUSE block, all five anchors: 'Attribution: 1: Completely incorrect attribution. 2: Significant attribution errors; misidentified threat actor. 3: Basic attribution; minor inaccuracies. 4: Mostly correct attribution. 5: Perfect attribution; clearly identifies the threat actor.' So in the Threat Actor block 'Attribution' measures SOURCE LINKING -- whether the generated text is traceable to the input article -- and NO anchor in that block mentions identifying a threat actor. In the Root Cause block 'Attribution' measures THREAT-ACTOR IDENTIFICATION and says so in three of its five anchors. Confirmed by two fetches on two URL renderings (arxiv.org/html/2603.09452v1 and arxiv.org/html/2603.09452), the second asked for both blocks whole with every numbered anchor and permitted to answer ABSENT or CANNOT READ. A one-sentence gloss from the first fetch, 'Attribution: Evaluates whether the generated context properly attributes information to the original article', is consistent with the fuller anchors. THE CLAIM IN CONFLICT, verbatim from this issue's third candidate_resolution: 'THE LOAD-BEARING PART IS THE WITHIN-TABLE CONTRAST, not the model gap: the same GPT-4o scores 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.612 on Content: Root Cause in the same table, so its 1.140 on threat-actor attribution is a deficit specific to attribution rather than a general inability to draft.' That contrast sets 1.140 against 3.612, and those two cells are NOT the same measurement. Taken at face value the two sources leave a reader with opposite impressions of whether mechanical IoC extraction is a solved problem. NEITHER SIDE IS PICKED, and this entry deliberately records that the conflict may dissolve on inspection, because three confounds are unresolved: (1) SYSTEM -- LANCE is regex pre-filter + LLM + human validation, src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs', so this may be a measurement of scaffolding value rather than a disagreement; (2) METRIC -- 97.6% is an F1, 0.82-0.88 are precision with no recall reported anywhere in src-0007 and no reason given for the omission; (3) CORPUS -- PRISM is 50 public threat reports, src-0007's material is an unnamed company's internal daily workflow of unknown relative difficulty. Neither paper cites the other. RESOLUTION PATH for a future cycle: recover recall/F1 from src-0007's released code (GitHub/HuggingFace per its abstract) to make the metrics comparable, and/or find any source running an unscaffolded LLM against PRISM or a LANCE-style scaffolded pipeline against CyberThreat-Eval. - (ioc-extraction-reliability) CODE-READING CONFLICT, opened by cycle 27's G2 re-verification of src-0017 (github.com/xschen-beb/CyberThreat-Eval). Same shape as ctr-0002 and ctr-0003: the stored quotations are exact, the characterisation built on top of them is not what the source does. THE STATE SAYS, in this issue's own open_question added at cycle 21: 'src-0017's evaluator matches predicted IoCs to ground truth with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions -- its own comments read (For prediction, if pred.lower() in ground truth or ground truth in pred) alongside (Exact match)'. The same two-directional characterisation was then repeated as settled fact in three scores.json rationales (ttp-attack-mapping-reliability, task-dependent-reliability-framing and extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis, cycles 22 and 26), in the form 'src-0017 shows src-0007's released IoC evaluator matches by two-directional SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT'. THE SOURCE SAYS OTHERWISE. stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/eval/eval_ioc.py was retrieved WHOLE for the first time this cycle (raw.githubusercontent.com/xschen-beb/CyberThreat-Eval/main/stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/eval/eval_ioc.py, fetch instructed to reproduce the entire file verbatim or write CANNOT READ). The EXECUTING code is ONE-DIRECTIONAL: 'true_positives = sum(any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) for pred in pred_list)', 'false_positives = len(pred_list) - true_positives', 'false_negatives = sum(not any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for pred in pred_list) for gt in gt_set)'. The two-directional variant ('(pred.lower() in gt.lower()) or (gt.lower() in pred.lower())') and the exact-match variant are EACH ENCLOSED IN A TRIPLE-QUOTED STRING LITERAL and never execute; the four lines cycle 21 quoted are the comment headers standing above those dead blocks. CONFIRMED AT A SECOND URL FORM, per the rule that a single negative verdict is unreliable: the IoC sub-README (raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/README.md) states the rule in prose, verbatim -- 'A prediction is considered a True Positive (TP) if pred.lower() in gt.lower() for any ground truth IOC from the same source'. Code and documentation agree with each other and against the state. WHY THIS IS NOT A PEDANTIC CORRECTION: the direction determines the SIGN of the bias, and every downstream use in this base assumed a single sign. Under the actual one-directional rule the leniency is ASYMMETRIC. It is LENIENT toward short or fragmentary predictions, since any prediction that is a substring of a longer ground-truth entry scores TP. It is STRICT against verbose predictions, since a prediction containing the ground-truth IoC plus surrounding text scores FALSE POSITIVE -- which is the characteristic failure mode of a free-form LLM extractor and is exactly the case the dead two-directional block would have scored TP. So src-0017.md's limitation 'A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality' is half right: relative to strict equality this matcher inflates on one axis and DEFLATES on the other, and no cycle may continue to cite it as unidirectional inflation. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY OF BLAME, since neither side is being silently picked: src-0017.md's own limitations bullet says only that 'the comments show substring matching in both directions', which is literally true of the comments, and it explicitly warned that 'the surrounding matching loop is not fully transcribed'. The .md file flagged its own uncertainty honestly; the open_question and the three scores.json rationales dropped that hedge and asserted the mechanism. This entry is filed against the assertion, not against the source file. TWO FURTHER PROPERTIES OF THE ACTIVE CODE, first-time observations from the same verbatim read, RECORDED AS OBSERVATION AND NOT USED TO SUPPORT ANY CANDIDATE. (a) Ground truth is built as a SET per source while predictions are kept as a LIST, so duplicate correct predictions each count as a separate true positive while false negatives are counted over the deduplicated ground-truth set; repeated correct predictions therefore inflate TP relative to a set-based count on both metrics. (b) Both sides are normalised by the same chain, verbatim 'item.replace("[", "").replace("]", "").replace("hxxp", "http").replace("hxxps", "https").replace("[.]", "[]").split(" - ")[0].strip()' then lowercased, within which the '[.]' to '[]' step is unreachable because both bracket characters have already been removed by the two preceding replaces. The first half is now DONE and is the content of this entry. The second half remains open and is recorded at src-0003.md line 141 as never stated by that paper, so it is probably unresolvable from the sources in this base. The ATT&CK-task scoring rule is a DIFFERENT file and is still unread; the repository's top-level listing (re-confirmed verbatim this cycle as .DS_Store, .gitignore, README.md, stage1_triage/, stage2_deep_search/, stage3_ti_drafting/) contains stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/, which is where it should be. - (consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode) FALSE-POSITIVE-CORRECTION CONFLICT, opened by cycle 39's G2 re-verification of src-0016 (Snyk, 'Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0: LLM Bug Repeatability', snyk.io blog, byline Liran Tal, 29 June 2026). THIS IS A NEW SHAPE AND THE TENTH IN THIS BASE'S DEFECT CLASS: A PRIOR CYCLE'S CORRECTION IS ITSELF WRONG. The disputed claim is not about the world and not about the source -- it is about this base's record of the source, and the check that produced it was a G2 exactly like this one. THE STATE SAYS, src-0016 index.json key_claims[4], entered by cycle 21 as a G2 CORRECTION: 'The string presented in key_claim 1 as a single verbatim quotation -- 80 of 161 unique-unmatched findings appeared in only one of five identical repetitions, while only 22 appeared in all five -- DOES NOT APPEAR ON THE PAGE in that form: the page reads Across all model configurations, 80 of 161 unique, unmatched finding signatures appeared in only one of five repeated runs, and the 22 appeared in all five figure is a distribution-table cell (5 of 5 runs = 22, 13.7%), not prose. It is a quotation error, not a factual one.' THE SOURCE SAYS OTHERWISE, AND BOTH SENTENCES ARE ON THE PAGE. Two fetches at cycle 39, the article URL and a ?print=1 rendering, each instructed to write ABSENT rather than infer and each explicitly told not to echo back a supplied string it had not found. The ?print=1 rendering returns BOTH, verbatim: (A) 'In plain terms, when Claude reported bugs outside the Snyk Code reference list, those extra reports were often inconsistent. Across 250 model runs, 80 of 161 unique-unmatched findings appeared in only one of five identical repetitions, while only 22 appeared in all five. But when Claude matched a reference finding, the behavior was much more stable: 134 of 158 unique reference-matched findings appeared in all five repetitions. That split is the core result of Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0.'; and (B) 'Across all model configurations, 80 of 161 unique, unmatched finding signatures appeared in only one of five repeated runs.' SO THE ORIGINAL CYCLE-15 QUOTATION IS EXACT AND ALWAYS WAS. Sentence (A) is the page's plain-terms summary paragraph and sentence (B) is its narration of the distribution chart; the page simply states the statistic twice in different words, and cycle 21 found (B), failed to find (A), and concluded from that failure that (A) had been spliced. IT HAD NOT BEEN. Cycle 21's subsidiary point is wrong for the same reason: '22 appeared in all five' is BOTH a prose clause in (A) AND a table cell ('5 of 5 runs | 22 | 13.7%'), not the cell alone. WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE, AND IT IS THE LARGER HALF OF CYCLE 21'S WORK: correction (b) of that same key_claim is FULLY CONFIRMED. Four tables exist on the page, the collection note claiming none did was false, and cycle 21's transcription re-verifies EXACTLY at cycle 39 -- Table 2 unique unmatched findings 5 / 6 / 36 / 60 / 54 and fully-stable shares 60.0% / 50.0% / 16.7% / 8.3% / 9.3% for Opus 4.6 Medium, Opus 4.6 High, Opus 4.7 Max, Sonnet 4.6 Medium, Sonnet 4.6 High; Table 4 precision 91.5 / 89.8 at recall 68.0 / 68.2 for the two Opus 4.6 configurations against precision 62.6 / 58.6 at recall 80.9 / 81.3 for the two Sonnet 4.6 configurations, with the Snyk Code SAST row at 100.0% F1 / recall / precision by construction; and every figure in key_claims[0] through [3] -- 80, 161, 22, 134, 158, 84.8%, 13.7%, 300 runs -- confirmed exact. SO CYCLE 21 WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE TABLES AND WRONG ABOUT THE QUOTATION, and only the quotation half is disputed here. NEITHER SIDE IS SILENTLY PICKED; note that one side is the page's own body text, returned by a rendering that was explicitly instructed not to confirm strings it had not found and that volunteered surrounding context nobody asked it for. ONE NEW FACT RECOVERED IN PASSING AND NEVER RECORDED BY ANY CYCLE: sentence (A) scopes the 80-of-161 statistic to 'Across 250 model runs', not to the 300 runs this base has always cited alongside it. 300 is the whole design ('Each configuration ran each task five times: 10 tasks x 6 configurations x 5 repetitions = 300 runs') and includes the 50 Snyk Code SAST baseline runs, which produce no model findings; the model-finding statistics are over 250 runs. Any future citation should say 250. METHODOLOGICAL BY-PRODUCT, AND IT IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE OF THE SINGLE-FETCH-ABSENT RULE BUT THE FIRST IN WHICH THE FALSE NEGATIVE FELL ON THE CORRECTING CYCLE RATHER THAN ON THE ORIGINAL: cycle 39's FIRST fetch of the plain article URL returned sentence (B) as ABSENT while returning sentence (A) as PRESENT -- the exact mirror image of cycle 21's result on the same page -- and the ?print=1 rendering returned both. Two honest fetches of one unchanged page disagreed about which of two real sentences exists. That is the mechanism that produced this defect, and it means rule (v) must be read as applying to a G2's own corrections and not only to the claims a G2 audits. RULE (xiii) IS VINDICATED AND SHOULD BE STRENGTHENED: it says a false contradiction is more expensive than a missed one because it is entered as a finding and inherited, and this entry is the proof -- cycle 21's false correction has been inherited and restated by every handoff since, including the one cycle 39 executed, which recommended src-0016 for re-checking precisely BECAUSE it 'carries a KNOWN quotation defect'. Eighteen cycles of trust in a defect that was not there. RESOLUTION PATH, TWO STEPS, NEITHER OF WHICH THIS ENTRY CLOSES ON ITS OWN. (ii) NOT DONE, AND THIS IS WHY THE ENTRY STAYS OPEN: state/knowledge/src-0016.md has not been read or amended by cycle 39 and may carry the same false correction in its own prose, where a reader who never opens index.json would meet it unqualified. A later cycle should read that file and append the correction there, then close this entry. - (extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis) OPERATIONALISATION CONFLICT, opened by cycle 42's G2 re-verification of src-0006 (arXiv 2509.23573, 'Uncovering Vulnerabilities of LLM-Assisted Cyber Threat Intelligence'), the stalest source in the base, last checked at cycle 18. THIS IS THE TWELFTH DEFECT SHAPE IN THIS BASE: the state's account of WHAT A MEASURED TASK IS, against the source's own operationalisation of it. Five successive cycles (33, 36, 37, 39, 41) named src-0006's never-read per-task scoring definitions as the highest-value unfetched item in this project and as the largest untested load-bearing assumption in it. They have now been read. THE RESULT IS GENUINELY MIXED AND BOTH HALVES MUST TRAVEL TOGETHER; A SUCCESSOR THAT CITES ONLY ONE HALF WILL MISREAD THIS ENTRY. HALF ONE, WHICH CUTS IN THE STATE'S FAVOUR AND IS REPORTED FIRST BECAUSE THIS BASE HAS A DOCUMENTED BIAS TOWARD FINDING DEFECTS. The long-standing worry was that 'all in F1' establishes only that the STATISTIC is constant across src-0006's nine commensurable rows, not that the MATCHING RULE is. THAT WORRY IS ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE: the rows do share one scoring form. Appendix B.3 ('Task Description') gives, verbatim, 'Affected Systems (F1): Binary decision per asset: is a listed host/application impacted by the described CVE/IOC set (yes/no).'; 'Attack Infrastructure (F1): Binary decision per indicator: determine whether an IP/domain/URL belongs to adversary C2 or delivery infrastructure.'; 'Malware Family Mapping (F1): Binary decision per candidate family: does observed behavior/artifacts match the family's signature (yes/no).'; 'IOC Normalization (F1): Binary correctness for canonicalizing raw IOCs (type+value) against gold forms.'; 'TTP Extraction (F1): Binary decision per candidate technique ID: is T#### evidenced (yes/no).'; 'False Flag Detection (F1): Binary decision: is an observed signature intentionally misleading (yes/no).'; 'Infrastructure Reuse (F1): Binary decision per linkage: does an IOC show reuse across events (yes/no).'; 'Relation Graph Building (F1): Binary decision per candidate relation triple (entity-relation-entity).' EVERY F1 ROW IS A BINARY PER-ITEM DECISION. THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROJECT THAT ACTUALLY READING A SCORING RULE HAS CONFIRMED A STATE ASSUMPTION RATHER THAN BREAKING IT, and the standing prior repeated in five rationales -- 'every single time a cycle in this project has actually read a scoring rule it has differed from what the state assumed, seven documented instances' -- MUST NOW BE RESTATED AS SEVEN OF EIGHT. A successor must not keep quoting the unqualified form. HALF TWO, WHICH IS THE CONFLICT AND IS WHY THIS ENTRY IS OPEN. THE STATE SAYS, extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis candidate_resolutions[1], status 'supported', route 1: a 'Contextualization stage mean of 0.636 (IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607) against an Attribution stage mean of 0.602 (TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511)', with the load-bearing argumentative move being that 'the best task in the subset is an Attribution-stage task' -- i.e. the proposed ordinal axis is LOCALLY INVERTED AT ITS STRONGEST PREDICTED POINT. THE SOURCE SAYS that this best task, TTP Extraction, is 'Binary decision per candidate technique ID: is T#### evidenced (yes/no)'. IT IS NOT EXTRACTION. It is binary verification of technique IDs that are SUPPLIED TO THE MODEL AS CANDIDATES. And the same holds across the subset: every row on BOTH stages is operationalised as a binary yes/no judgement over supplied items. THEREFORE THE COMMENSURABLE SUBSET DOES NOT VARY THE ORDINAL AXIS'S INDEPENDENT VARIABLE AT ALL. The rungs of the proposed ordering are mechanical extraction, classification, attribution and generation; src-0006's nine F1 rows collapse all of them into binary classification by construction. The 'Contextualization' and 'Attribution' labels are the PAPER'S OWN CTI-PIPELINE-STAGE labels -- Appendix A.1-A.4 -- and they are subject-matter groupings, not operationalisations of the extraction-versus-reasoning distinction. WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT, SCOPED PRECISELY SO THIS IS NOT OVER-READ. The candidate's NEGATIVE CONCLUSION -- that the ordinal axis is NOT SUPPORTED -- survives, and arguably survives more strongly: a measurement in which the independent variable has been eliminated by construction supplies no support for the ordering. What does NOT survive is route 1's POSITIVE ARGUMENT, which is the part doing the work. 'The ordering is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point' requires TTP Extraction to be an instance of the attribution-reasoning rung; as operationalised it is not, so the inversion is between two binary-verification tasks and is not evidence about the rung ordering. The 0.034 stage gap is likewise a gap between two subject-matter groupings measured under one common task form, which is a different and much weaker finding than the one the candidate states. THIS MATTERS DISPROPORTIONATELY BECAUSE ROUTE 1 IS THE ONLY SURVIVING ROUTE ON THIS CANDIDATE: route 2 is already void under ctr-0008, which established that src-0007's 1.140 cell is a SOURCE-LINKING score and not an attribution-identification score. IT IS NOT THE SAME TASK. src-0006's is a binary yes/no verification over supplied candidate technique IDs; src-0007's is free-form technique generation scored by EXACT technique-ID set intersection with no partial, parent or sub-technique credit (established from executing code at cycles 31 and 32). NEW SUB-RULE, to be applied to every long arXiv HTML source in this base: WHERE A PAPER'S HTML IS LONG ENOUGH TO TRUNCATE, AN ABSENT VERDICT ABOUT ANY APPENDIX IS WORTHLESS, AND THE CHEAPEST WORKING ROUTE IS TO FETCH AN EARLIER VERSION WHOSE HTML IS SHORTER. - (ttp-attack-mapping-reliability) THREE COHEN'S KAPPA VALUES ARE POOLED INTO A SINGLE '0.68-0.76 BAND' ACROSS THIS BASE, AND THEY ARE THREE DIFFERENT STATISTICS. Opened by cycle 46's G2, which was the FIRST G2 ever run on src-0021 (added cycle 43, never re-checked). This is the ctr-0013 metric-identity shape applied to an agreement statistic rather than to an F1, and its proximate cause is the ctr-0012 shape: a subordinate clause of the very sentence this base quotes was dropped when the quotation was stored. WHAT THE STATE SAYS. src-0021 key_claims[1] stores, as its TRAM-Clean agreement quotation, verbatim and ending exactly there: 'For TRAM-Clean, we report the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases'. It then concludes, verbatim: 'trained human annotators on PARENT-level ATT&CK techniques land in the 0.68-0.76 band -- substantial on Landis and Koch, but well short of the near-perfect agreement that an exact-ID scoring rule implicitly presumes. Two independent teams, two corpora, one conclusion.' ttp-attack-mapping-reliability open_questions[1] carries the same framing verbatim: 'TWO TEAMS, TWO CORPORA, ONE BAND: 0.68-0.76'. WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS. An exact-string ask against https://arxiv.org/html/2605.25836v1 on 2026-08-01 returned the sentence COMPLETE, and it does not end where this base ends it: 'For TRAM-Clean, we report the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases (i.e., cases that reached the adjudication stage).' The parenthetical is the DEFINITION of 'contested cases' and it was confirmed a SECOND time in a separate exact-string ask on the literal string '(i.e., cases that reached the adjudication stage)', which returned PRESENT with the same full sentence. THE DEFECT. Restricting a pairwise kappa to cases that reached adjudication restricts it to the subset on which the annotators had ALREADY DISAGREED OR FLAGGED DIFFICULTY -- a selected hard subset, not a sample of the annotation task. An agreement coefficient computed on such a subset is not the same quantity as one computed over all items, and there is no general direction of bias one may assume without knowing the selection rule, so it cannot even be signed as 'conservative'. THE THREE VALUES NOW SEPARATE CLEANLY, AND NO TWO ARE THE SAME STATISTIC: (1) src-0020's 0.68 is a MEAN OVER 114 PER-TECHNIQUE Cohen's kappa values, reported with no confidence interval, verbatim 'we reached a mean inter-annotator agreement of kappa=0.68 across 114 techniques'; (2) src-0021's 0.76 is a single kappa over ALL sentence-level annotations of TTPrint-Bench under double-annotation with adjudication by 3 annotators; (3) src-0021's 0.74 is a PAIRWISE kappa over the ADJUDICATION-SELECTED CONTESTED SUBSET of TRAM-Clean. A mean-of-per-class-kappas, a whole-corpus kappa and a hard-subset pairwise kappa are three different estimands. THE PHRASE 'ONE BAND' AND THE PHRASE 'ONE CONCLUSION' BOTH OVERSTATE, and the specific inference that must not be drawn is that three roughly equal numerals corroborate one another: their near-equality is not evidence of convergence, because they are not estimating the same thing. WHAT IS NOT DISTURBED, STATED NARROWLY SO THIS ENTRY IS NOT OVER-READ IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. All three NUMERALS are exact and all three quotations except the truncated one re-verified PRESENT; the underlying qualitative point -- that trained annotators on PARENT-level ATT&CK labelling agree substantially but well short of the near-perfect agreement an exact-ID scoring rule presumes -- SURVIVES ON EACH VALUE INDEPENDENTLY, and survives most strongly on src-0020's, which is the only one of the three measured over an unrestricted item set AND the only one that reports the tail (57.0% of techniques clearing kappa>=0.7, i.e. 43% below it). THE STANDING PROHIBITION FROM open_questions[1] IS ALSO UNDISTURBED AND IS REINFORCED: an agreement statistic is not an accuracy baseline, and none of these three discharges the human-baseline question. A SECOND, LESSER DEFECT FOUND BY THE SAME G2 AND RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN IN ITS OWN ENTRY BECAUSE IT CHANGES NO CLAIM: src-0021 key_claims[0] stores the backbone list as one continuous quoted run beginning 'GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Open-source models include Qwen 3 235B and DeepSeek v3.2'. The source has TWO sentences and the first BEGINS 'Closed-source models include GPT-4o, ...' -- confirmed verbatim by exact-string ask. The stored run drops that leading clause without an ellipsis while retaining the parallel clause of the following sentence, producing a sentence that does not exist in the paper. The MODEL LIST IS CORRECT AND COMPLETE and nothing downstream changes; it is a splice, recorded so the twelve-way defect taxonomy stays honest about its own instances. RESOLUTION PATH, FOUR STEPS. (i) DONE AT CYCLE 46: append a key_claim to src-0021 in state/knowledge/index.json recording the complete sentence with its parenthetical, the three-estimand separation, and the splice -- this is src-0021 key_claims[4]. (ii) DONE AT CYCLE 46: append the same to state/knowledge/src-0021.md. THIS IS THE STEP ctr-0011, ctr-0012, ctr-0013 AND ctr-0014 EACH LEFT UNDONE ON THEIR OWN SOURCE FILES; cycle 46 did it for ITS OWN entry at the same time as (i), which is the cheapest moment to do it and the reason four predecessors failed is that they deferred it. THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE ctr-0014 STEP (ii), WHICH IS ABOUT src-0003.md AND REMAINS UNDONE.
